Episode list, show notes, subscribe links, and host bio, live at a free kodely.site URL in minutes.", "targetKeyword": "build a podcast website with AI", "category": "Use-Cases", "bodyHtml": "

What a Good Podcast Website Actually Needs

Your podcast already lives on Spotify and Apple Podcasts. So why build a website for it at all? Because a website is the one place you fully control, no algorithm, no platform rules, just your show presented the way you want it. A good podcast site needs a handful of things done well:

  • An episode list with real show notes — titles, descriptions, guest names, and timestamps for each episode.
  • A host or about section — who is behind the mic and why anyone should trust them.
  • Subscribe links — one-click buttons to Spotify, Apple Podcasts, YouTube, or wherever your audio actually lives.
  • A contact section — for guest pitches, sponsors, or listener mail.

That is it. No plugins, no CMS logins, no theme marketplace. Just a clean, fast site that makes your show look as good as it sounds.

The Honest Part: Kodely Builds the Site, Not the Podcast Hosting

Worth saying plainly before you start: Kodely does not host your audio files, and it does not generate an RSS feed for podcast apps. That job belongs to a dedicated podcast host, whatever you already use to get episodes into Apple Podcasts and Spotify in the first place.

What Kodely builds is the front door: the marketing and informational website around your show, the episode list, the show notes, the host bio, and embedded players or subscribe buttons pointing at wherever your episodes already live. Think of it as the site listeners land on from a link in your bio, not the infrastructure that delivers the audio itself.

The One-Prompt Approach

You do not need a designer or a web developer to get a real podcast site live. You describe it in one message, in plain English, and Kodely writes the actual code, real components, not a template with your logo dropped in.

A Real Example Prompt

Here is the kind of prompt that gets you a genuinely usable result on the first try:

“Build a podcast website for my show called Founder Signal, a weekly interview podcast about early-stage startups. I want a hero section with the show name and a one-line description, a grid of the 6 most recent episodes with title, guest name, and a short summary for each, an about section with my bio and a photo placeholder, subscribe buttons linking to Spotify and Apple Podcasts, and a simple contact section for guest pitches. Use a dark, modern look with an accent color.”

That single description is enough for Kodely to lay out sections, write placeholder copy where you have not supplied real content yet, and structure the episode grid as reusable components.

What Kodely Actually Generates

Behind the live preview, Kodely writes a real Vite plus React 19 plus TypeScript plus Tailwind CSS v4 application, actual .tsx component files built on hand-built UI primitives, not a static HTML mockup. You can open the code view at any point and see the real source files it produced. Every episode card, every button, every section is a proper component, which is exactly why editing it later in chat works so cleanly: Kodely is changing real code, not repainting a template.

Customizing Your Podcast Site Through Chat

Once the first version is up, refine it the same way you started it: describe the change. “Make the episode cards two columns on mobile,” “add a newsletter signup above the footer,” “swap the accent color to green,” “add a Patreon link next to the subscribe buttons,” each request edits the actual components behind the scenes. If a generation does not compile, you are not charged for it, and every successful generation is saved as a checkpoint you can roll back to for free if a later change goes somewhere you did not want.

Publishing to a Live URL

When the site looks right, hit Publish. One click puts it live at a real public address, something like foundersignal.kodely.site, included at no extra cost, with no separate hosting step. Every publish is automatically scanned for accidentally leaked secrets or API keys before it goes live, so you are not shipping something you will regret. There are no custom domains yet, so for now your show lives at its kodely.site subdomain, plenty for a link in your show notes or social bio.

FAQ

Do I need any coding experience?

No. You describe the site in plain English and Kodely writes the actual React components. You can view and copy the generated code if you want to, but you never have to.

Will this host my podcast audio or submit it to Apple Podcasts?

No. Kodely builds the website: episode list, show notes, subscribe links, about page. Your episodes still need a dedicated podcast host to generate the RSS feed that Apple, Spotify, and other apps read.

Can I use my own domain name?

Not yet. Every site published today lives at a free subdomain of kodely.site.

What does it cost?

Signing up gets you 750 free credits, no credit card required, which is enough to build and publish a site like the one above. Beyond that, credits are metered from real AI cost, and a build that fails to compile is never charged. Top-ups start at $9 for 500 credits, with $40 for 2,500 credits and $90 for 6,000 credits. Credits never expire.

Can I download the code and host it myself?

Not yet, there is no code export or zip download today. You can view and copy source files in the code view, and publishing to your kodely.site URL is built in and free.

Build your podcast website free, describe your show, get a real site, publish it in minutes. Start building on Kodely.
